newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cask of tequila is key clue in Mexican drug scandal.
newsitem.headline: Cask of tequila is key clue in Mexican drug scandal.

text.p: The case against Mexico's fallen drug czar and his alleged trafficker associate hinges in part on a barrel of tequila, Mexican authorities say.

Mexico's Attorney General's Office (PGR) disclosed key evidence on Monday in its case against Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, the country's top anti-drug official until he was arrested last week on charges of working for Amado Carrillo Fuentes, head of the powerful Juarez drug cartel.

Topping a list of items turned up in a search of Gutierrez's luxury Mexico City aparment, which allegedly was paid for by the drug baron, was a wooden barrel of tequila inscribed with the name "Amado Carrillo."
Authorities said they also turned up a letter addressed to "Don Amado Carrillo" from a prison inmate, an AK-47 assault rifle and $10,000 in cash.

Gutierrez, who formerly led an austere life in the city of Guadalajara, shared the apartment with his girlfriend while Carrillo occasionally used an apartment in the same building in one of the capital's most exclusive neighbourhoods, the PGR said. Uniformed guards protect the entrance to the building around the clock.
The PGR said 36 associates of the general had been removed from their posts and that more heads could roll in the scandal.
